hook: A Dutch attic cleanout uncovered 25 documents stolen 10 years ago.

sections.voiceover: A Dutch attic cleanout uncovered 25 documents stolen 10 years ago.
sections.visual_cue: Extreme close-up of aged parchment documents resting inside a dusty storage box.

sections.voiceover: An archivist stole 25 records from the Netherlands' National Archives in The Hague. The thief used these 16th-century records from the Dutch VOC trading company as loan collateral. Where did those 25 stolen archives end up?
sections.visual_cue: Exterior shot of the Netherlands' National Archives building in The Hague, shifting to dimly lit archive racks.
b_roll: Netherlands National Archives exterior The Hague

sections.voiceover: But the family found these 25 historic VOC documents inside a cheap Action cardboard box.
sections.visual_cue: Close shot of hands opening a worn cardboard box labeled Action in an attic space.

sections.voiceover: Art detective Arthur Brand recovered all 25 centuries-old manuscripts. Brand and the Amsterdam police recovered a 15th-century letter and early 17th-century VOC records. The stolen artifacts were safely returned to the Netherlands' National Archives.
sections.visual_cue: Art detective Arthur Brand inspecting old manuscripts alongside official law enforcement officers.

sections.voiceover: Ten years after vanishing, 25 stolen documents returned to The Hague.
sections.visual_cue: Wide camera pan across the exterior of the National Archives building in The Hague under clear daylight.
